intent.task: Comprehensive security audit of smart contracts with specific focus on reentrancy vulnerabilities, access control mechanisms, invariant violations, and oracle manipulation attacks

protocol_intent.summary: AI-powered smart contract security analysis protocol featuring x402-compatible budget management for agent services, ERC-8004 style policy registries, and intent-based approval systems for autonomous security agents.

invariants.description: Budget solvency: Locked funds must always cover all settled and pending obligations. The contract must never allow settlement amounts to exceed the locked budget balance.
invariants.formal: lockedBalance >= totalSettled + sum(pendingIntents[i].amount) for all i

invariants.description: Intent approval consistency: The view function approveIntent() and the state-changing approveIntentWithEvent() must return identical boolean approval decisions for identical intent parameters to prevent state divergence.
Policy-authorized settlement: Budget settlement can only be triggered by agents registered in SRPPolicy with active authorization for the specific intent type, preventing unauthorized fund drainage.
invariants.formal: settle(intent) requires SRPPolicy.isAuthorized(msg.sender, intent) == true ∧ SRPPolicy.isActiveAgent(msg.sender) == true

invariants.description: Event-state correspondence: approveIntentWithEvent must emit exactly one IntentApproved or IntentRejected event per invocation, and the event parameters must match the actual approval decision and consumed budget amount.
invariants.formal: ∀ calls: emitCount ∈ {1} ∧ event.decision == internalDecision ∧ event.caller == msg.sender

invariants.description: Budget immutability during pending settlement: Locked budget amounts associated with pending intents cannot be withdrawn or reallocated until the intent is either settled or explicitly rejected.

access_control_rules: Only the budget owner can lock and unlock funds in SRPBudget
Only agents registered in SRPPolicy with valid ERC-8004 credentials can call approveIntentWithEvent
Only the SRPPolicy contract or its designated oracle can update agent authorization statuses
Settlement execution requires dual authorization from both the budget contract (sufficient funds) and policy contract (intent approval)
trust_assumptions: AI agents registered in the policy registry act according to their declared capabilities and do not collude to drain budgets
The x402 payment rail provides accurate settlement confirmations
The approveIntentWithEvent function is called atomically with off-chain agent execution to prevent intent replay
Budget oracle prices (if any) are accurate and tamper-resistant
protocol_intent.economic_model: Pay-per-use security analysis with escrow-based budget management. Users lock funds in x402-compatible budget contracts. Autonomous AI agents consume locked funds based on policy-approved intents (audit tasks). Settlement occurs after service delivery with event-logged approval trails. Fees are deducted from locked amounts upon successful intent fulfillment.

key_components.name: SRPBudget
key_components.role: Holds locked funds, manages budget lifecycle (lock/settle/refund), executes ETH transfers to agents and owners

key_components.name: SRPPolicy
key_components.role: ERC-8004 policy registry managing agent registration, skill authorization, and intent approval logic

attack_surfaces: Reentrancy via low-level .call transfers in settleBudget and refund before state updates
State divergence between approveIntent view function and approveIntentWithEvent state-changing function (INV-002 violation)
Replay attacks on intent approval if approveIntentWithEvent lacks idempotency storage writes
Unauthorized settlement execution bypassing SRPPolicy agent authorization (INV-003 violation)
Double spending via race conditions between settled, refundableWei, and lockedAmount state variables
Access control bypass on registerAgent allowing malicious agent registration
External call to untrusted owner address in settleBudget enabling reentrancy and fund drainage

plan.action: Test reentrancy protection (CEI pattern), verify caller authorization against SRPPolicy registry, validate budget solvency checks (locked >= settled + amount)
plan.reason: Highest risk score (29), performs external ETH transfer to owner with 5 state writes after potential reentrancy point, critical for fund safety

plan.action: Test reentrancy guards, verify refund amount calculation against refundableWei storage, ensure atomic state updates preventing double refunds
plan.reason: External call to arbitrary msg.sender with 4 writes, classic reentrancy target with complex accounting state

plan.action: Verify storage writes mark intent as processed (prevent replay), validate event emission matches boolean return (INV-004), test state consistency with approveIntent view function (INV-002)
plan.reason: 0 writes detected but must prevent replay; if view function approveIntent calls state-changing _isSkillAllowed, causes state divergence

plan.action: Test access control restrictions (only owner/policy admin), verify agent authorization state initialization, check for agent ID collision or spoofing
plan.reason: External function with 5 state writes controlling entire authorization graph; unauthorized registration bypasses all security

plan.action: Audit state mutation logic (2 writes detected in internal function), verify it doesn't corrupt view function behavior or enable storage collision attacks
plan.reason: Internal function with writes is anti-pattern; may cause unexpected side effects when called by view functions

plan.action: Verify settleBudget validates msg.sender against SRPPolicy.isAgentAuthorized before execution, test policy contract upgrade scenarios
plan.reason: Critical trust boundary; settlement must require dual authorization per INV-003

plan.action: Invariant testing: lockedAmount >= settled + refundableWei at all times; verify no path allows settlement exceeding locked budget (INV-001)
plan.reason: Multiple writers (2 each) on critical accounting variables risk insolvency through double counting
